concepts.def: Pigments suspended in drying oil, allowing slow blending and glazing, used by Old Masters and contemporaries like Lucian Freud.
Thick application of paint creating visible texture and brushmarks, used dramatically by Van Gogh and Frank Auerbach.
Application of thin translucent layers over a dried underlayer, deepening colour and luminosity in oil painting.
Monochrome or limited-palette layer establishing tonal structure before full colour is applied.
Wet-into-wet painting method completed in a single session, favoured by Impressionists such as Monet.
Fast-drying water-based paint developed in mid-twentieth century, used by David Hockney in his California pool paintings.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Art, Craft and Design — a core area of A-Level Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Art, Craft and Design brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Art, Craft and Design.
